parallel.requirements: Recognized the prompt as a clean-room reverse-engineering task: write a new codebase matching the provided compiled dstask binary by observing behavior, not by wrapping or copying the original.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent created a probe helper and notes directory, then delegated behavior characterization across 12 exploration children. The delegated deliverables were notes by command or behavior area, while the parent implicitly kept future implementation ownership.
parallel.implementation: No replacement program source, build script, or packageable implementation was produced. The workspace mostly accumulated notes, docs, the original executable, and helper scripts.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Ten child note reports returned through the AgentSwarm result, but two research scopes were aborted. The packaged artifact contains notes and the original materials rather than a buildable implementation.
parallel.verification: Children performed many local behavior probes against the binary, but the parallel run never reached integrated differential testing of a new executable because there was no implementation.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The run timed out with two child agents aborted, missing disk-format and table-renderer notes, and a final artifact that failed official compilation before tests could run.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same clean-room reverse-engineering task and the need to write a replacement executable from observed binary behavior and bundled documentation.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The single main agent sequentially owned exploration, design, implementation, and testing. Its todo state still had implementation, differential tests, and compile script pending late in the run.
serial.implementation: The serial agent reasoned toward a Go implementation with stdlib-only hand-rolled YAML after dependency download failed, but it did not finish writing source before cancellation.
serial.integration_and_delivery: No child results had to be integrated. The delivered artifact contained README, docs, .git metadata, LICENSE, and the original executable, with no replacement code.
serial.verification: The serial run performed behavior probes and dependency checks, but no integrated tests of a new executable occurred because implementation remained pending.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The run timed out during continued probing. The official artifact was invalid and failed compilation with all 1589 tests not run.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized that the task required a clean-room replacement executable and delegated observation of binary behavior.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same clean-room replacement requirement and directly probed the binary and docs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement misunderstanding separates the outcomes; both knew the need for original source, but neither delivered it.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed into a 12-child AgentSwarm for behavior notes; the children were scoped to research deliverables, not implementation modules.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept one owner for the whole task and maintained a todo list where implementation, differential testing, and compile script remained pending.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent its parallelism on breadth-first research handoffs, while serial kept a single sequential critical path; both postponed implementation too long.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs were detailed for each behavior area and asked for exact notes, but they did not define implementation interfaces because implementation was not delegated.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept findings in one context and adjusted its implementation approach when dependency download failed, deciding to hand-roll YAML with the standard library.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The main contrast is not a missing cross-agent contract; parallel transferred research scopes, whereas serial accumulated implementation context locally.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel did not start a replacement codebase; the final artifact member list is notes, helper scripts, docs, repository metadata, and the original executable.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial analyzed implementation details and dependency options, but its todo state still listed implementation and compile script as pending.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial was closer to an implementation design, while parallel had broader notes; neither converted observations into source files.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel cancellation interrupted active child agents and the parent received an AgentSwarm result with 10 completed and 2 aborted children.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child lifecycle; the main single-agent turn was cancelled directly near the end of probing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lost child deliverables through a child-result lifecycle boundary; serial failed through unfinished single-agent progress.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children shared temporary scratch space and one child observed clobbered capture files, but that issue was rechecked and did not become the retained final-delivery failure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one workspace without child write collisions; its final artifact still lacked an implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had observable shared-scratch interference plus unassembled notes, while serial had no concurrency write boundary; both final trees lacked source.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children verified observed behavior locally, but no replacement executable existed for integrated acceptance testing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial performed many probes and dependency checks, but likewise had no replacement executable for integrated acceptance testing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The verification gap is shared: both official evaluations completed but failed at compile time with every testcase not run.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used the full budget in swarm mode, timed out, and had no remaining budget after the provider attempt.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also used the full budget and timed out, with no subagents and no completed source artifact.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both failed under the same budget envelope, but parallel's closure included aborted child work while serial's closure was a direct single-agent interruption.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official completed status.json evaluations are both failures: parallel and serial each report compile_failed, solution_passed false, and 1589 not_run tests. The prompt-level and trajectory-level comparison still shows a real process difference, because parallel lost two child research deliverables at cancellation while serial simply remained in a single-agent exploratory path. That difference did not produce a discordant official outcome because neither attempt delivered buildable replacement source.
parallel_contributors: The 12-child swarm produced broad notes but two assigned research scopes were aborted before final notes existed.
The final artifact contained notes, helper scripts, documentation, repository metadata, and the original executable, not replacement source.
serial_contributors: The serial run kept implementation ownership in one agent but still had implementation, differential tests, and compile script pending late in the run.
The final artifact also lacked replacement source and failed official compilation.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial reasoned about a Go implementation and hand-rolled YAML after network dependency failure; parallel concentrated on distributed notes and did not reach that coding step.
Neither attempt contains enough implementation behavior for ordinary coding defects to explain a pass/fail split.
evaluator_effects: No evaluator anomaly is needed to explain the outcome; both artifacts were invalid before tests ran.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; one retained parallel-side process loss only

candidates.reason: Parallel assigned research notes to children while the parent implicitly retained later implementation; missing final source alone does not prove no implementation owner under the taxonomy.
No multiple component implementations were produced, so there was no concrete integration contract or integration owner to omit.
The parallel run had no complete component set or buildable source needing only final assembly; it remained at research notes.
There were not owned implementation, build, test, and delivery stages whose end-to-end transition was left ownerless.
No single mandatory preflight or oracle step gated all productive work; the parallel run launched many behavior probes concurrently.

The child investigations overlapped, and two did not complete a clean first phase; the directly evidenced adverse boundary is cancellation of active children, not serial-phase completion before late implementation.
Implementation was postponed, but the same episode is more directly evidenced as active child cancellation; no separate allocation event with a distinct consequence is proven.
The 12-child breadth and timeout are screening signals, but high fan-out plus timeout alone does not satisfy the label when the direct observed boundary is cancelled active children.

The aborted disk-format and table-rendering tasks were substantive but not uniquely demonstrated as oversized relative to siblings; cancellation, not overbroad child scope, is the observed failure boundary.
The child briefs included the clean-room constraints, target binary, docs, helper, and note deliverables; no known requirement omitted from an executed brief made the work unusable.
Parallel children were not delegated independently built components expected to interoperate, so there was no missing implementation interface contract.
No specific known finding is shown to disappear through a summary or transfer and cause repeated work or a wrong action by the parent.
The completed child summaries were large, but there is no parent decision point after receiving them where their bulk is shown to prevent reduction before a next action.
No received child handoff is shown to describe a superseded workspace or requirement state that the parent then used incorrectly.
No incompatible completed child reports reached the parent and remained unadjudicated at an integration decision.
The parent did not make an observable whole-task completion claim based on partial results; timeout and artifact packaging occurred without an accepted implementation.
There is no replacement child or retry that restarted without inherited findings and repeated prior work.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: The parent launched a 12-child AgentSwarm with explicit notes deliverables, then the active turn was cancelled and the swarm result reported 10 completed and 2 aborted children. The disk-format and table-rendering children were still working before their note deliverables finalized.
candidates.realized_consequence: Two assigned behavior-research deliverables, disk-format notes and table-renderer notes, remained unfinalized and unavailable to the parent before the final non-compilable artifact was packaged.
candidates.near_match_reason: The aborted children might suggest missed takeover, but the trace shows cancellation at closure and no separate parent decision point after the abort; the direct lifecycle boundary is early termination.

candidates.reason: No complete implementation candidate or compatible component set existed for final placement; notes and partial research are not a promotable deliverable.
No child implementation change was merged after integrated verification, and no integrated verification of replacement source occurred.
No delegated implementation was completed or retrievable; the delegated work was research notes, not buildable code that the parent failed to join.
No verifier child produced a concrete finding that was trapped below the parent; the aborted children were research probes, not verifier returns.
The child aborts occurred as part of terminal cancellation, and the trace lacks a later parent window where takeover was possible but omitted; this is covered by Early Child Termination.
The parent received completed child summaries only at the final swarm result after cancellation; no later decision point shows visible completed results being ignored.

The parent was awaiting the AgentSwarm result, but the trace does not show a separate available-progress inspection opportunity ignored before timeout; the same chain is better labeled as early child termination.
Parallel children wrote separate note files by topic and did not create competing implementation files or overlapping component designs requiring reconciliation.
No two live agents are shown editing the same source, config, or final deliverable file and then reconciling a concurrent change.
No non-entry source module was produced and then replaced, deleted, or rewritten by another live agent.
No required executable or entry-point source was produced and overwritten while another agent owned or used it.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replaced multiple current final outputs or invalidated another agent's final-tree work.
Shared temporary-file interference was observed and then rechecked with unique names, but it did not cause a concrete unstable final implementation or provenance failure.
No child-generated artifact, cache, fixture, or tool was consumed by another actor as stable reference input and contaminated the final result.
